comparison: Perfect agreement on PLMGraph-Inter architecture (C35-C58). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. Reviewers explicitly affirm the method is 'very well detailed' and 'carefully written,' directly validating OpenEval's assessment of the architectural claims and SE(3) invariance properties.

Perfect agreement on performance comparisons with baselines (C41-C42, C68-C72). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. Reviewers confirm 'various comparisons suggest that PLMGraph-Inter performs substantially better' and describe evidence as 'solid,' aligning with OpenEval's assessment despite noting potential test set contamination.

Perfect agreement on structure quality impact (C92-C96). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. Reviewers implicitly acknowledge these findings without challenge, noting the method works 'when accurate experimental structures are available,' consistent with OpenEval's assessment of the DTM-score threshold analysis.

Strong agreement on ablation studies (C97-C104, C188). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. Reviewers explicitly state 'the ablation studies convincingly demonstrate that the chosen model architecture is appropriate,' directly validating OpenEval's assessment of component contributions including PLM embeddings.

Disagreement on de-redundancy analysis (C105-C110). OpenEval evaluates as SUPPORTED, but peer reviewers evaluate as UNCERTAIN, raising critical concern that 'A more challenging test would be to restrict the test set to pairs of interacting proteins such that *none* of the chains are separately similar to monomers present in the training set,' suggesting current analysis may not fully address data leakage.

Agreement on DHTest/DB5.5 comparisons (C116-C121) with shared caveats. Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. Both acknowledge test set contamination issues that compromise CDPred comparisons, with reviewers noting 'DHTest and DB5.5 are not de-redundant with the training sets of CDPred and GLINTER.'

Perfect agreement on AlphaFold-Multimer comparison limitations (C130-C136, C144). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. Reviewers acknowledge the training set date discrepancy and unfair comparison conditions, validating OpenEval's assessment of the authors' transparent acknowledgment of these critical limitations.

Partial disagreement on 50% precision threshold (C137-C140, C43). OpenEval evaluates as SUPPORTED with caveats, peer reviewers evaluate as UNCERTAIN. Reviewers note the threshold is 'a potentially useful heuristic' but raise concern that gains in 'DockQ-failed' and 'precision-failed' bins 'are based on knowledge of the ground truth final structure, and thus are not actionable in a real use-case.'

Related claims about complementarity with AlphaFold-Multimer (C43, C141). OpenEval evaluates as UNCERTAIN due to unfair comparison conditions. Peer reviewers also express uncertainty, noting that for heterodimers 'when AFM has low confidence, PLMGraph-Inter improves precision by (only) about 3% on average,' questioning practical significance.

Perfect agreement on docking applications (C44, C147-C156). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. Reviewers do not challenge docking results and note the work 'will be of interest to researchers working on protein complex structure prediction,' implicitly accepting utility for downstream applications.

Perfect agreement on homomeric vs heteromeric performance differences (C75-C82). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. Reviewers acknowledge the method 'works both for homodimers and heterodimers' without challenging the authors' explanations for differential performance.

Perfect agreement on dataset construction and de-redundancy approach (C60-C62, C164-C165). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. Reviewers explicitly commend this aspect as 'more careful than can be said of most works in the field of PPI prediction.'

Agreement on HADDOCK limitations (C157-C159, C142-C143). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. Reviewers implicitly acknowledge these limitations, with one noting the method 'may be useful in cases where AlphaFold-Multimer performs poorly,' recognizing the method has limitations.

Agreement on future directions and limitations (C160-C163, C142-C143). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. Reviewers do not contest the authors' acknowledgment that heteromeric PPIs need improvement, consistent with OpenEval's assessment.

Agreement on limitations assessment (C142-C144). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. Reviewers implicitly acknowledge these limitations without challenge, validating OpenEval's assessment that honest limitation acknowledgment strengthens credibility.

Agreement on training set contamination implications (C144). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. Reviewers acknowledge the training set date discrepancy issue, consistent with OpenEval's assessment of this logical inference.

Agreement on PLM embedding contribution (C188-C190). Both evaluate as SUPPORTED. Reviewers' statement that 'ablation studies convincingly demonstrate that the chosen model architecture is appropriate' encompasses the dramatic improvement from adding PLM embeddings noted by OpenEval.
